newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends little changed vs US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends little changed vs US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed almost unchanged at 8.2910 on Monday from last Friday's 8.2908 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai with a wait-and-see sentiment dominating the market, traders said.
The weighted average price on Friday was 8.2906.
Traders said many bankers stayed on the sidelines on Monday, waiting for the release of first half 1997 foreign trade data, expected around the middle of the month.
The yuan opened unchanged at 8.2908 and hit a low of 8.2930 early in trading. It then moved in a narrow range between an intraday high of 8.2905 and 8.2910 for most of the session.
Trading was less active than on Friday with most business done at 8.2908, traders said.

One trader said the market expected China's first-half foreign trade surplus to be much stronger than at the same time in 1996 but the expected positive news had already been partly factored into the yuan's upward trend in the past few months.
"The trade surplus is expected to be high and therefore to support the yuan," he said.
"But it has partly been factored into the local currency, and is unlikely to push the yuan much higher," he said.
"Even the foreign trade data is very strong, the key 8.2900 resistance level would seem a difficult resistance point," said a second trader. "This is making traders cautious."
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move around 8.2910 on Tuesday.
The yuan closed up at 7.2730 from 7.2850 against 100 Japanese yen and down at 1.0701 from 1.0695 against the Hong Kong dollar.
